payload:
Implementation plan for the standard-revenue case:
1) Scope
- Define and confirm expected behavior for the standard-revenue flow, including inputs, calculation rules, outputs, UI/API touchpoints, persistence/reporting effects, and any acceptance criteria.
- Update only the components necessary to support the standard-revenue case end to end; avoid unrelated refactors.

2) Discovery and impact analysis
- Identify where revenue-case logic currently lives (frontend forms, backend services, calculation modules, validation layers, database schema/config, reporting/export paths).
- Map existing revenue case variants and determine whether standard-revenue is new, missing, or partially implemented.
- Review tests and fixtures covering adjacent revenue scenarios to reuse patterns.

3) Implementation steps
- Add or update domain/model definitions to represent the standard-revenue case consistently.
- Implement backend/business-rule logic for standard-revenue calculations and validations.
- Update API contracts/serializers/controllers as needed so the case can be created/read/processed.
- Update frontend/UI flow if applicable to expose/select/display the standard-revenue case and resulting values.
- Add or adjust persistence/configuration/migrations only if the case requires new stored attributes or enum values.
- Ensure reporting/export/audit paths handle the case without errors.

4) Assumptions
- Standard-revenue behavior can be expressed within existing revenue-processing architecture.
- No major schema redesign is required; at most, additive changes such as enum/config updates.
- Acceptance criteria can be inferred from existing revenue-case conventions unless clarified by product/business rules.

5) Risks
- Ambiguity in the exact calculation rules or edge-case handling for standard-revenue.
- Breaking existing revenue cases if shared logic is modified without adequate regression coverage.
- Inconsistent handling across backend, UI, and reporting layers if all touchpoints are not updated.
- Enum/schema changes may require careful migration/backward compatibility handling.

6) Validation approach
- Unit tests for calculation logic, validation rules, and serializers/models.
- Integration/API tests for create/read/process flows involving standard-revenue.
- UI/end-to-end tests for the user path selecting and submitting the standard-revenue case, if applicable.
- Regression tests for existing revenue cases to confirm no behavior changes.
- Manual verification of edge cases, error states, and reporting/output formatting.

7) Deliverables
- Code changes implementing the standard-revenue case.
- Test coverage for new and impacted flows.
- Short implementation notes documenting assumptions, any migrations/config changes, and known edge cases.

Suggested execution order: confirm requirements/expected rules -> inspect current revenue flow and impacted components -> implement model/business logic -> wire API/UI/persistence changes -> add tests -> run regression and e2e validation.
